name: Is there a difference between pool demolition and pool fill-in?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between pool demolition, pool removal, and pool fill-in?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between pool demolition, pool removal, and pool fill-in?

acceptedAnswer.text: These terms are often used loosely, which causes confusion during bidding. Pool demolition is the breaking and removal of some or all of the shell. Pool fill-in means the cavity gets backfilled after the shell is broken. Pool removal is often used as the umbrella term for the whole process, from demolition through backfill and grading. Some contractors use the words interchangeably, but the actual work can be very different. That is why homeowners should not rely on labels alone. They should ask exactly what happens to the shell, how much concrete is removed, whether compaction is included, and what final condition the site will be left in. In Los Angeles, where project scopes can vary widely by property, clear definitions are essential for comparing estimates fairly.
